chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: Regarding a woman who vowed to perform tawaf on four [parts of the Ka'bah], he said: 'She performs one circuit for her hands and one circuit for her feet.'

key_terms.أُسْبُوعاً: A full circuit (720 degrees, consisting of two circuits of 360 degrees each in some interpretations, or simply a full round)
key_terms.نَذَرَتْ: She vowed (feminine form of nadhr, a religious promise)

ai.seo_question: How is a vow to perform tawaf on 'four' parts of the Ka'bah interpreted and fulfilled in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the principle of *takhayyur* (choice) in fulfilling specific vows, where the Imam clarifies that 'four' refers to four distinct sections rather than a literal count of circuits. By dedicating one full circumambulation to the 'hands' (upper parts) and another to the 'feet' (lower parts), the vow is satisfied with two complete rounds, reflecting the scholarly tradition of interpreting vague numerical vows through physical division of the Ka'bah's structure.
